title: Amplification of Weak Randomized Decision
statement: Let $E$ be a verifier model closed under majority amplification: whenever a Boolean verifier is efficient for $E$, so is the majority of polynomially many runs on polynomial-length random blocks. If a language $L$ has an efficient verifier whose acceptance probability on members and rejection probability on nonmembers are each at least $1/2+\min\{1/6,(|x|+1)^{-c}\}$ for some natural number $c$, then for every natural number $d$, $L$ has an efficient verifier whose corresponding probabilities are each at least $1-2^{-((|x|+1)^d+1)}$.
hypotheses_covered: $E$ is closed under majority amplification with polynomial block and repetition lengths
$L$ has a weak randomized verifier for some natural number $c$
